newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Novartis wants to be in Hungary top 50.
newsitem.headline: Novartis wants to be in Hungary top 50.

text.p: The Hungarian unit of diversified pharmaceuticals and chemicals maker Novartis said it hopes turnover in 1997 will place it among the leading companies in Hungary.

"With an estimated total turnover in health care and agribusiness of over 18.6 billion forints in 1997, Novartis Hungary will rank among the top 50 companies of the country and will play a dominant role in the markets of the specific products," Novartis said in a statement on Tuesday.

The company, the Hungarian subsidiary of Novartis created when Ciba and Sandoz merged last year, said its health care products started appearing on the Hungarian market on March 1 and agricultural products should be available in June.

"The seasonality of agriculture...explains why Novartis Agribusiness, including crop protection, animal health, field crop as well as flower and vegetable seeds, will start its operations in Hungary the 1st of June 1997," it said.

Novartis Hungary plans to generate a turnover of more than 10.2 billion forints from healthcare in 1997, it said, adding, "Novartis will account for approximately 10 percent of the total Hungarian health care market".

In health care more than 75 percent of Novartis's sales come from prescription drugs, while OTC drugs account for 13 percent, ophthalmic and eye care products for six percent and generics for three percent.
